title: Apollo Company Enrich
description: Look up a company's full Apollo.io profile from its domain
whenToUse: Pick when you ALREADY HAVE a company domain and need its full Apollo profile: industry, revenue, headcount, funding and contact details. Use it to enrich a known domain; discovering companies by criteria, or enriching people, are different jobs.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Trigger. The domain usually templates from upstream output.

outputs.name: company
outputs.description: The enriched profile, or null when Apollo has no match

outputs.name: found
outputs.description: Whether a match was found. A miss is a normal result, not an error.

domain.title: Company Domain
domain.description: Domain of the company to enrich, e.g. 'google.com'

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.

authRole.description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.

package.name: gtm
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# Two vendors, one package: Apollo.io for company and people data, Hunter.io for email.
# One credential each, one base URL each, no SDKs.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gtm/`.

name: gtm
displayName: Go To Market
description: Company and people discovery, enrichment and email verification
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775374180/gravity/icons/apollo.jpg

features:
  - Apollo company and people search, with filters
  - Apollo company and people enrichment
  - Hunter email discovery, finding and verification

allowedHosts:
  - api.apollo.io
  - api.hunter.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [page]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.apolloCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: apolloCredential
displayName: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io master API key for people and organisation search
documentationUrl: https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apollo.io master API key, required for the search endpoints
    placeholder: ""
credentials.hunterCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: hunterCredential
displayName: Hunter.io
description: Hunter.io API key for email discovery, verification and enrichment
documentationUrl: https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hunter.io API key, found under API in your Hunter dashboard
    placeholder: ""

shared.apollo.yaml:
# What every Apollo call shares.
#
# The key travels in the `x-api-key` HEADER, which is `apiKeyHeader`, an executor
# capability. `Cache-Control: no-cache` is sent because the retired client sent it: Apollo
# is documented as caching search responses, and dropping the header would silently change
# which results come back.

credential: &credential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: x-api-key
  value: "{{ credentials.apolloCredential.apiKey }}"

headers: &headers
  Cache-Control: no-cache

# NOTE for the bodies below: every filter is a comma-separated config field turned into the
# array Apollo wants, with
#
#   String(config.x || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
#
# and an EMPTY array is left out of the body rather than sent, because Apollo reads an empty
# filter as "match nothing" rather than as "no filter". That is why each body is built by an
# expression that assembles only the keys that have values, instead of a static object.
shared.hunter.yaml:
# What every Hunter call shares.
#
# TWO auth styles, and that is Hunter's doing rather than ours: `/discover` takes the key in
# an X-API-KEY header, every other endpoint takes it as an `api_key` query parameter. Both
# are executor capabilities, so each call names the one its endpoint wants.

queryCredential: &queryCredential
  scheme: apiKeyQuery
  param: api_key
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

headerCredential: &headerCredential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: X-API-KEY
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

# Hunter wraps every payload in `data` and reports failures in `errors`, sometimes with a
# 200. Without this a quota error would emit an empty result and read as "not found".
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response.errors && response.errors.length)"
  message: "return response.errors.map(e => e.details || e.id).join('; ')"

# A LinkedIn URL to the handle Hunter wants. split/join rather than a regex, because the
# expression sandbox takes no regex literal: everything after /in/, up to a ? or #, with any
# trailing slash removed.
linkedinHandle: &linkedinHandle >-
  return String(config.linkedinHandle || '').trim()
    .split('/in/').slice(-1)[0]
    .split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    .split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-1)[0] || ''

files.api/events.yaml:
# A miss returns 200 with no organization, so `found` tests for an id rather than for a
# key: Apollo sometimes returns a stub object with nothing in it.

- emit: company
  from: response
  value: "return response.organization || null"

- emit: found
  from: response
  value: "return !!(response.organization && response.organization.id)"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One GET. The domain is a query parameter, so it is percent-encoded by the executor.

- name: enrich
  method: GET
  url: https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/organizations/enrich
  credential: { $ref: apollo#credential }
  headers: { $ref: apollo#headers }
  query:
    domain: "return String(config.domain || '').trim()"
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [domain]
  properties:
    domain:
      type: string
      title: Company Domain
      description: Domain of the company to enrich, e.g. 'google.com'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, domain]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. The domain usually templates from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: company
    type: object
    description: The enriched profile, or null when Apollo has no match
  - name: found
    type: boolean
    description: Whether a match was found. A miss is a normal result, not an error.

credentials:
  - name: apolloCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Apollo.io
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: ApolloCompanyEnrich
kind: PromiseNode
name: Apollo Company Enrich
category: Go To Market
color: "#F5D800"
description: Look up a company's full Apollo.io profile from its domain
whenToUse: >
  Pick when you ALREADY HAVE a company domain and need its full Apollo profile: industry,
  revenue, headcount, funding and contact details. Use it to enrich a known domain;
  discovering companies by criteria, or enriching people, are different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: true

# One vendor. The package allows Hunter too, for its other five nodes.
allowedHosts: [api.apollo.io]
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    domain: apollo.io
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    found: "return output.found === true"
    company: "return typeof output.company.name === 'string'"
